name: Senior Dog Checklist
description: A checklist to help owners care for an aging dog with regular vet checks, mobility support, the right diet, and a comfortable home.

items.text: Schedule more frequent senior wellness exams
Ask about bloodwork and screenings for older dogs
Keep vaccines and parasite prevention up to date
Discuss dental health and professional cleanings
Track findings and follow-up steps after each visit
items.note: Ask your vet how often your senior dog should be seen

items.text: Provide soft, supportive bedding
Add non-slip rugs on slippery floors
Use ramps or steps for cars and furniture
Keep nails trimmed for better footing
Offer gentle, regular exercise suited to your dog
Feed a diet suited to a senior dog's needs
Measure portions to keep weight healthy
Provide easy access to fresh water
Adjust food height or texture if eating is hard
Discuss supplements only with your vet first
Keep a calm, predictable daily routine
Provide warm, draft-free resting spots
Offer more frequent potty breaks
Keep grooming gentle and check skin and coat
Give mental stimulation with easy games and contact
Appetite, thirst, and weight shifts
Stiffness, limping, or trouble rising
Lumps, bad breath, or dental problems
Confusion, restlessness, or sleep changes
Vision, hearing, or bathroom habit changes
items.note: Report new or worsening signs to your vet promptly

items.text: Note daily comfort, mobility, and mood
Track good days versus difficult days
Discuss pain management options with your vet
Adapt the home as your dog's needs change
Keep open conversations with your vet about care
This checklist is general information for owners, not veterinary advice; an aging dog's needs depend on its breed, size, and health, so always consult a licensed veterinarian
items.note: For any emergency, contact your vet or an emergency animal hospital immediately

faq.q: When is a dog considered a senior?
faq.a: It varies by breed and size, with larger dogs often reaching senior age sooner than small ones. Ask your veterinarian when your dog enters its senior years and how care should change.

faq.q: How often should a senior dog see the vet?
faq.a: Many older dogs benefit from check-ups more than once a year so issues are caught early. Your veterinarian can recommend a schedule and any screenings based on your dog's age and health.

faq.q: How can I help my aging dog with mobility?
faq.a: Provide soft bedding, non-slip rugs, ramps for cars or furniture, and gentle regular exercise. If your dog is stiff or slow to rise, talk to your veterinarian about supportive options.

faq.q: Should I change my senior dog's diet?
faq.a: Older dogs may need different calories or nutrients, and weight control matters for joint and heart health. Ask your veterinarian whether a senior diet or portion change is right for your dog.

faq.q: Is this senior dog checklist printable?
faq.a: Yes. Print it or download the PDF, track vet visits and changes, and use it to keep your aging dog comfortable and well cared for.
